verdict.rationale: Modal's own SDK lets a developer attach a specific GPU type to a Function through the `gpu` argument. Its docs claim containers spin up in 1–2 seconds and that resources are available in seconds without quota requests, so the core goal of running code on a GPU quickly is delivered programmatically. However, the model is serverless GPU containers rather than a provisioned 'instance', and there is no evidence of console-based provisioning, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: console/UI GPU provisioning, a persistent on-demand instance lifecycle, and independent or hands-on corroboration of time-to-running-code.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: You can pick a specific GPU type for your Function via the `gpu` argument.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
Access the right resource for your workload in seconds without quota requests or long lead times.
The [Modal](https://modal.com/) Python SDK allows you to deploy high-performance serverless applications and programmatically interact with the Modal platform.
